data.title: Hurricane Simon strengthens to Category 4 off Mexico coast
data.description:
Hurricane Simon strengthened into a powerful Category 4 storm off Mexico's Pacific coast on Saturday, threatening destructive winds, storm surges and potentially deadly flooding as it approaches landfall.

The US National Hurricane Center said Simon was located about 115 miles (185 km) south-southwest of Manzanillo on Saturday morning, packing maximum sustained winds of 150 mph (240 kph) as it moved northward.

Simon is expected to approach the west-central coast of Mexico as a major hurricane late Saturday or early Sunday, and some additional strengthening remains possible before landfall, the NHC said.

A hurricane warning was in effect for portions of Mexico's Pacific coast south of the beach resort of Puerto Vallarta, including the area around Manzanillo, Mexico's largest Pacific port. A tropical storm watch was in effect farther south toward Lazaro Cardenas.

The NHC urged residents in the warning area, which also includes the Islas Marias archipelago offshore, to rush preparations to protect life and property.

“Simon has strengthened incredibly quickly, and that’s what makes storms like this so dangerous,” said AccuWeather meteorologist Dan Pydynowski.

“Strong winds could damage homes and businesses, while flooding and mudslides could wash out roads and make it difficult for emergency crews to reach some communities. Even after the storm passes, power outages and damaged infrastructure could make recovery challenging.”

Mexican authorities warned that heavy rainfall was expected in the states of Guerrero, Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco.

The NHC said Simon was expected to produce 10 to 20 inches (25 to 51 cm) of rain across portions of southwestern Mexico through Sunday, with isolated totals of up to 30 inches (76 cm) possible in parts of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco. The rainfall could trigger life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in mountainous areas.

A storm surge is expected along the coast near and to the east of where the center makes landfall, accompanied by large and destructive waves, the NHC said. Swells generated by Simon are expected to affect portions of Mexico's southwestern and west-central coast over the coming days, creating dangerous surf and rip current conditions.

Simon is forecast to be near or just inland of Mexico's west-central Pacific coast on Sunday.

Last week, Hurricane Polo made landfall on the Baja California Peninsula as a Category 2 storm, toppling trees and utility poles, flooding streets and causing other property damage.

data.title: America's Gig Workers Turn to an Old-School Union — WSJ
data.description:
By Paul Kiernan

LOS ANGELES — When Margarita Peñalosa began driving for Uber and Lyft in 2017, eight hours a day was enough to cover living expenses and send cash to family in Colombia. Now she said it takes 12-hour days.

"The cost of driving is twice what it was when I started," Peñalosa said.

Peñalosa's frustrations go a long way to explaining why she and more than 50,000 California ride-share drivers recently signed cards to join the newly formed California Gig Workers Union.

Organizers have told drivers the union could help them secure more take-home pay in one of the nation's least affordable states, where the country's highest gas prices and a growing fleet of driverless taxis are undercutting the economics of gig work.

The union marks the biggest U.S. effort yet to organize a workforce that numbers in the millions nationwide. Ride-share drivers are free to set their own schedules, giving them flexibility to care for children or work other jobs. But since they are classified as independent contractors rather than employees, gig workers lack traditional labor protections in most of the U.S. Those include minimum wage laws, workers' compensation and collective-bargaining rights.

Instead of an hourly wage, Uber and Lyft drivers are paid by the ride. To receive trip requests, they must be "online" with the ride-share app. Drivers are offered upfront rates determined by the platforms' proprietary algorithms and must learn to quickly distinguish worthwhile trips from low-paying ones.

They don't get paid for time spent behind the wheel waiting for trip requests, or driving back from a distant drop-off with an empty back seat.

A growing number of mostly Democratic cities and states are extending new labor protections for gig workers. Massachusetts certified the nation's first union for ride-share drivers in May, a few months ahead of California. Illinois could soon follow after Gov. J.B. Pritzker signed a law in August that will allow Uber and Lyft drivers to unionize.

California and Massachusetts also guarantee drivers a minimum wage based on the time they spend actively driving passengers, though the rest of their time remains uncompensated.

In Oregon, Portland's city council considered a proposal earlier this year to cap the "take rate," or share of a passenger's fare that goes to Uber and Lyft, at 20%. New York City, Washington state and Minnesota have adopted rules in recent years guaranteeing drivers earn a minimum amount per mile.

Despite the new protections, mounting overhead costs are eating into gig workers' earnings.

They pay vehicle-related expenses, including insurance, repair and maintenance costs that have all outpaced inflation in recent years. And they are especially hit by gasoline prices that are up more than 50% this year nationwide. California drivers were recently filling up at about $6.31 a gallon for regular gas, the highest average of any state, according to AAA.

Lyft declined to comment on driver pay, but a spokesman said the company "does well when drivers do well." An Uber spokesman said the company's drivers make more than $34 an hour in California "when actively working" — meaning the time between accepting a ride and dropping off a passenger — an increase of about 17% since 2019.

After factoring in their operating costs, like gasoline, and the time they spend online but not actively serving customers, several ride-share drivers in Los Angeles said their actual hourly earnings often fall below the state's $16.90 minimum wage.

"The gas is killing me," said Artur Gevorkyan, 46, who has been driving for Uber off and on since 2015.

He made $1,006 before taxes and expenses for about 22 hours of active driving time in one of his better recent weeks, according to a review of his pay statement. Measured by active driving time, that means he was grossing nearly $45.50 an hour.

But after including nearly 30 additional hours he spent online for Uber — time Gevorkyan considers working hours — his pretax income for that same week would come out to less than $19.50 an hour.

His expenses include a $600 monthly payment on his 2019 Infiniti QX60, nearly $800 every six months for the insurance and close to $70 for gas on a typical 250-mile day.

Gridwise, an analytics platform used by hundreds of thousands of Uber and Lyft drivers, estimates that average gross pay nationwide was $24.38 an online hour in the second quarter. That was up 7.3% from a year earlier but down about 10% from 2021, when drivers' earnings peaked amid a postpandemic labor shortage.

Driver earnings have lagged behind in Los Angeles, among the first cities to allow driverless Waymo taxis to compete for customers since 2024. More than 900 of the self-driving taxis now roam the streets here, doing the work of thousands of human drivers and posing what many analysts consider a threat to ride-share platforms — and drivers.

In contrast to their fierce opposition around the U.S. to workers being classified as employees, Uber and Lyft haven't fought the unionization push. That is partly because the California bill that allowed drivers to unionize was part of a legislative bargain that also reduced the ride-share companies' insurance costs.

Union organizers made their pitch to drivers at airport ride-share parking lots in Los Angeles, San Francisco and other cities, often over free coffee, doughnuts or pizza. In addition to pay and benefits, the union has said it could help appeal so-called deactivations, whereby the companies cut off drivers' access to the apps for alleged violations of their rules, unsafe driving or other reasons.

California Gig Workers Union spokesman Tim Sandoval said the organization will eventually represent all of the estimated 300,000 to 350,000 ride-share drivers in the state.

Sam Gutierrez, 54, broke down in tears as he described having to apply for Medicaid and food assistance this year for the first time in his life, even though he drives 10 to 11 hours a day for Uber and Lyft in the Inland Empire east of Los Angeles. He said he typically grosses $140 to $150 a day, minus about $30 of gas for his Ford Focus.

"It's crazy the way we're living right now," he said. "I just went on medication, my blood pressure went up so drastically."

data.title: AI Could Weaken Ethereum Security as Cryptographic Risks Grow, Vitalik Buterin Warns
data.description:
Buterin urged developers to prepare for potential AI vulnerabilities in both conventional and quantum-resistant cryptography, while cautioning Ethereum and other cryptocurrency holders against rushing to move their funds between wallets.

In a post on X on October 8, Buterin identified lattice-based cryptography as a particular area of concern, arguing that AI-assisted mathematical research could uncover weaknesses that researchers have not yet discovered. His comments add another dimension to the debate over blockchain security, which has increasingly focused on whether existing cryptographic methods can withstand advances in quantum computing and artificial intelligence. The Block reported that Buterin recommended reducing exposure to potentially vulnerable cryptography without triggering unnecessary wallet transfers.

AI Advances Could Challenge Lattice-Based Cryptography

Buterin warned that mathematical advances accelerated by AI could undermine assumptions about the security of lattice-based cryptography. These techniques underpin several emerging security technologies, including the Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm (ML-DSA) and fully homomorphic encryption (FHE).

Vitalik warns that rapid AI advances could undermine lattice-based and elliptic-curve cryptography sooner than expected, challenging assumptions about quantum threats. Source: @VitalikButerin via X

ML-DSA is a digital signature standard designed to resist attacks from quantum computers, while FHE allows computations to be performed on encrypted data without first decrypting it. Both technologies have applications beyond cryptocurrency, including secure communications, privacy systems and data processing.

Buterin cautioned that cryptographic systems considered secure today could face new risks if AI helps researchers discover more efficient ways to solve the mathematical problems on which they depend.

“There is a good chance that the concrete security of lattices will take serious hits from the next two years of AI math,” he wrote.

His concern centers on the possibility that AI systems could identify mathematical shortcuts that significantly reduce the computing resources required to attack existing encryption methods. Such discoveries would not necessarily make every lattice-based system immediately vulnerable, but they could force developers to reconsider security parameters and key sizes.

Buterin compared the potential development with improvements in integer factorization, where advances in algorithms made it possible to solve certain mathematical problems more efficiently than earlier methods suggested. He argued that similar breakthroughs could emerge in the study of elliptic curves and lattices.

However, his comments describe a potential future threat rather than a demonstrated cryptographic break. The warning does not establish that AI systems can currently derive private keys from Ethereum wallets or defeat deployed lattice-based encryption.

Ethereum's Roadmap Favors Hash-Based Signatures

The warning also helps explain Ethereum's growing preference for hash-based cryptographic techniques in parts of its long-term technical roadmap.

Buterin said Ethereum's lean roadmap has moved toward a “hash-only” approach for signatures and proofs, avoiding lattice-based components where hash-based alternatives are feasible. He specifically referenced Winternitz One-Time Signatures (WOTS) and SPHINCS+, two hash-based signature schemes.

Vitalik Buterin predicts Ethereum will support cheaper, high-volume transactions with stronger privacy within two years, as stated at OKX NOW in Singapore on October 6, 2026. Source: @WuBlockchain via X

Hash-based signatures rely on cryptographic hash functions, which transform input data into fixed-length outputs. Their security does not depend on the same mathematical structures used by elliptic-curve or lattice-based systems. Buterin considers this distinction important because AI might discover exploitable properties in structured mathematical problems that researchers have not yet identified.

He argued that hash-based constructions should be preferred wherever practical, particularly if lattice-based alternatives require substantially larger parameters to maintain comparable security.

Nevertheless, the approach has limitations. Hash-based signatures do not provide a universal replacement for every cryptographic function. Public-key encryption, for example, requires additional mathematical structures that allow authorized users to encrypt and decrypt information securely.

Buterin acknowledged that challenge, noting that encryption underpins secure messaging, anonymizing networks, and other services beyond blockchain infrastructure. He suggested that developers using structured encryption systems should adopt more conservative security parameters and consider significantly larger keys where necessary.

The broader objective is to prepare cryptographic infrastructure for unexpected mathematical advances rather than assume that techniques considered resistant to quantum attacks will automatically remain secure against AI-assisted research.

Buterin Advises Against Rushed Wallet Migrations

Despite the potential risks, Buterin explicitly discouraged cryptocurrency holders from making immediate, unplanned wallet transfers.

“I don't recommend anyone scramble to move their funds to new wallets today,” he wrote, emphasizing the need to assess AI-related cryptographic risks without creating additional security problems.

One precaution he endorsed was keeping funds in addresses that have never been used to conduct transactions, provided doing so is straightforward. In commonly used wallet designs, a fresh address can help limit public exposure of the corresponding public key until it is revealed through a transaction.

That distinction matters because public keys and wallet addresses are not interchangeable. Depending on the address format and transaction history, an address may not directly expose the public key, although transaction activity can reveal it. Reducing public-key exposure may therefore offer a useful precaution against certain potential attacks, but it does not guarantee protection against every cryptographic vulnerability.

Buterin also recommended conducting multisignature wallet confirmations off-chain where possible. Multisignature systems require multiple approvals to authorize transactions, and keeping individual signatures off-chain can reduce the information exposed publicly during the approval process.

For privacy-focused applications, he advised developers to avoid placing encrypted notes directly on-chain when an off-chain alternative is available.

His caution reflects the operational risks involved in moving digital assets. Incorrect addresses, compromised devices, faulty wallet configurations, and mistakes during migration can cause irreversible losses.

“I personally have lost more money in botched migrations than I have lost in all hacks combined,” Buterin wrote.

The message is therefore not that users should ignore cryptographic risks, but that any security transition should be carefully planned and implemented.

AI Security Risks Extend Beyond Ethereum

Buterin's warning comes amid a wider debate about whether AI could accelerate the discovery of vulnerabilities in digital infrastructure. Ethereum researcher Justin Drake has separately urged the cryptocurrency industry to prepare for the possibility that AI could undermine elliptic-curve cryptography, including the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) used by many cryptocurrency systems.

Vitalik Buterin warns that AI-driven mathematical breakthroughs could weaken ECDSA signatures used by Bitcoin and Ethereum wallets sooner than expected. Source: @pete_rizzo_ via X

These concerns overlap with the industry's preparations for quantum computing, which could threaten widely used public-key cryptographic methods if sufficiently powerful quantum machines become available. AI and quantum computing present different technical challenges, however, and progress in one field does not establish that the other can break current encryption.

The discussion also highlights the importance of distinguishing theoretical vulnerabilities from demonstrated attacks. No successful AI-driven break of Ethereum's deployed cryptography was established by Buterin's warning. The immediate issue is whether rapid advances in mathematical reasoning could shorten the time developers have to adapt existing security assumptions.

The debate has also generated disagreement over the urgency of the threat. While some researchers advocate early preparations, the possibility of a breakthrough does not establish when, or whether, a practical attack will become feasible.

Buterin Sees AI as Both an Opportunity and a Risk

The cryptographic warning followed Buterin's October 6 appearance at the OKX NOW conference in Singapore, where he discussed AI's potential role in Ethereum's future.

According to OKX's conference recap, the event explored how artificial intelligence, blockchain infrastructure and financial services could converge. Buterin's broader vision includes AI agents interacting directly with blockchain applications, identifying opportunities and executing transactions with less dependence on conventional user interfaces.

He has also described a future in which Ethereum transactions become cheaper, and privacy protections improve as the ecosystem develops over the next two years. AI agents could eventually act as both trading counterparties and application developers, with automated systems negotiating and matching opportunities through on-chain infrastructure.

However, these prospective benefits depend partly on secure execution, reliable transaction authorization, and safeguards against malicious instructions or software vulnerabilities. Greater automation could reduce friction for users, but it could also introduce new risks if agents misunderstand instructions or interact with compromised applications.

The two discussions point to a central challenge for Ethereum: AI could make blockchain applications more accessible and capable while simultaneously increasing the importance of cryptographic security.

For now, Buterin's recommendations focus on preparation rather than emergency action. Developers should assess cryptographic assumptions, favor hash-based signatures where appropriate, and strengthen parameters for systems that rely on structured mathematical problems. Cryptocurrency holders, meanwhile, should avoid rushed wallet migrations and prioritize carefully implemented security measures.

Whether AI ultimately produces the mathematical breakthroughs Buterin anticipates remains uncertain. His warning nevertheless places cryptographic resilience among the issues blockchain developers must consider as AI capabilities continue to advance.

data.title: Flight disruptions growing after missile attack on Saudi airport
data.description:
Saudi Arabia is grappling with a surge in flight disruptions after a blast at the international airport in the kingdom’s capital, Riyadh, wounded many people and led to evacuations on Saturday, according to two regional officials.

A missile struck a passenger terminal and many people were wounded, one of the officials said. They spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren’t authorized to speak to the media. Ambulances were seen rushing toward the airport.

Flights to Riyadh diverted elsewhere, the Flightradar24 tracker said, almost four hours after the last flight landed at 2:05 p.m. Kuwait Airways said it was canceling flights because the airport had closed. Canada’s embassy advised citizens to avoid all travel to the airport, noting “ongoing military activity.”

King Khalid International Airport has been targeted multiple times in the week since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighboring Yemen. The Houthis claimed responsibility for the earlier attacks, including one Wednesday that killed a Sudanese national.

A resident said he heard explosions in Riyadh

There was no immediate Houthi statement Saturday. The Saudi government-run Center for International Communication, which oversees foreign media in the kingdom, didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

A Riyadh resident, Ahmed Sayed, told The Associated Press he heard at least two loud explosions that rocked the capital.

The airport issued a terse alert telling passengers to check their flight status with airlines before heading to the airport. At least 225 flights at the airport had been canceled over the past 24 hours, according to flight-tracking site FlightAware.

Fighting in Yemen between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces has escalated, with the Saudi-led coalition providing air support for government forces in an attempt to reverse recent Houthi gains along the Red Sea.

The rebels' gains gave them better surveillance of shipping on a corridor that's a crucial alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has been attacking ships.

Though the Houthis have told the AP and others they are only targeting Saudi shipping as part of a blockade in retaliation for one imposed on them, concerns about wider attacks persist. The Houthis previously attacked other ships after the war in Gaza began, calling it solidarity with Palestinians. A U.S. bombing campaign ended that.

Trump ‘not happy’ but no sign of new support

The Saudis have sought support from the U.S. and other allies as its airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure have come under attack. Officials said U.S. assistance has included intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for the latest offensive.

On Friday, as he left the White House, U.S. President Donald Trump was asked about the attacks on the Riyadh airport and told reporters, “It’s not good” and “I’m not happy.” But there has been no immediate sign of U.S. military support to respond to the attacks.

The Saudi and Omani foreign ministers spoke by phone about the importance of “supporting diplomatic solutions to de-escalate tensions” in the region, the kingdom said Saturday. Oman, which lies across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran, has played a mediator role at times in the region.

Meanwhile, Saudi authorities warned the public this week that "filming, publishing or sharing information related to countering missiles and drones and their impact sites exposes you to legal liability.”

Flight disruptions are growing

This week, the Houthis warned global airlines “for the last time” about the potential consequences of operating in Saudi airspace, which they described as a theater for their military operations.

Air India, FlyDubai, Lufthansa Group and Pakistan International Airlines have been among the airlines suspending flights to and from Riyadh and other Saudi airports for the next few days.

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency has expanded its guidance on Saudi airspace, noting the Houthis’ ability to strike targets deeper inside the kingdom, including Riyadh, and a “greater focus on aviation infrastructure.”

The missile and drone attacks and interception efforts “create an increased risk of misidentification of civil aircraft,” it said.

In Thursday’s attack, the Saudi national carrier said one of its aircraft was damaged while it was on the ground, with no passengers on board.

data.title: Bitcoin ETF inflows hit $3 billion in eight days as institutions return
data.description:
US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in approximately $3 billion in net inflows between September 17 and September 25, 2026. That stretch ranks among the strongest buying periods since the funds launched in January 2024.

The burst did something months of grinding could not. It pushed the year's flow tally out of the red.

Hedge funds, often cast as the fast money behind ETF surges, appear to have played only a minor role this time. The buying looks more like a broad institutional return than a trading desk making a short-term bet.

The peak week alone delivered $2.4 billion in net inflows. That was the largest weekly haul since October 2025.

BlackRock's IBIT led the pack with around $1.2 billion during that peak week. Fidelity's FBTC added roughly $702 million, while ARK 21Shares' ARKB brought in about $295 million.

The biggest single day came on September 21, 2026, when inflows hit nearly $999 million.

The rebound matters most against where flows stood earlier in the year. By mid-July, the funds were sitting on a year-to-date deficit of about $5.8 billion.

By late September, that hole had become a modest net positive of about $934 million.

The flows lined up with Bitcoin's price recovery. During the period, Bitcoin traded between $82,000 and $87,000.

Zoom out and the third quarter looks even stronger. Q3 2026 recorded $6.34 billion in Bitcoin ETF inflows, the highest of any quarter this year.

Cumulative net inflows since launch reached approximately $57-58 billion by early October 2026. Total assets under management sat around $105-110 billion over the same window.

The party did not last. Net outflows resumed in early October 2026, including a $244 million outflow on October 8.

When the spot ETFs debuted in January 2024, they offered something new. Traditional investors could get Bitcoin exposure through a brokerage account, no crypto exchange or private keys required.

Who is buying shapes how durable a rally might be. Hedge fund flows often tie to basis trades, where funds buy ETF shares and short futures to capture a price gap. That kind of buying can unwind quickly once the spread closes.

Broader institutional demand tends to be stickier. If allocators are adding Bitcoin as a portfolio slice rather than a trade, the money is less likely to sprint for the exit at the first wobble.

The late-September data leans toward the second scenario.

For investors, the clearest signal is a shift in sentiment. Wiping out a deficit of about $5.8 billion suggests institutions still see Bitcoin as a legitimate portfolio holding, not just a speculative side bet.

The concentration in BlackRock's IBIT also stands out. With around $1.2 billion of the peak-week inflows, the largest issuer kept widening its lead over Fidelity and ARK 21Shares.

Still, the October outflows serve as a reminder against reading too much into any single week. A $244 million exit on October 8 shows that sentiment can flip as fast as it arrived.

Bitcoin's price range also deserves attention. Inflows clustered while Bitcoin recovered into the $82,000 to $87,000 band.

What to watch next is whether early October outflows prove to be a pause or a turn. If the year-to-date total of about $934 million slips back toward negative territory, the September surge will look more like a relief rally than a trend.

If inflows resume and cumulative totals push past the approximately $57-58 billion mark, the case for steady institutional adoption gets stronger.

data.title: SEBI turns bond ratings into a consumer-friendly traffic-light system
data.description:
In a move to make bond investing easier for retail investors, market regulator SEBI has introduced a mandatory Credit Risk-o-Meter for debt securities. Issuers and Online Bond Platform Providers (OBPPs) must display the colour-coded risk meter in offer documents, abridged prospectuses, private-placement memorandums, advertisements, and the web and mobile platforms of OBPPs.

The framework covers listed and proposed-to-be-listed non-convertible securities, commercial papers, securitised debt instruments, security receipts and structured debt or market-linked debentures, whether issued through public issues or private placements. The provisions will come into force 45 days after the October 7, 2026, circular.

The pictorial representation is not new to the industry. This colour-coded Risk-o-Meter is used in mutual fund disclosures. SEBI introduced product labelling for mutual funds more than a decade ago and subsequently developed the current Risk-o-Meter framework. All mutual fund schemes must display a six-level Risk-o-Meter, ranging from Low to Very High risk, which is recalibrated monthly based on the underlying portfolio. The new bond Credit Risk-o-Meter adopts a similar colour-coded approach, moving from green for the lowest credit risk to red for the highest risk of default.

What is it?

While a mutual fund Risk-o-Meter captures multiple risks, including market, interest-rate, liquidity and credit risks, the new Credit Risk-o-Meter focuses exclusively on the credit risk associated with a debt security. It is intended to help small investors understand the risk of an issuer failing to meet its financial obligations.

Traditionally, investors have relied on credit ratings assigned by credit rating agencies (CRAs) such as Crisil, ICRA, CARE Ratings and India Ratings. While institutional investors and experienced market participants are familiar with rating symbols such as AAA, AA and BBB, retail investors may find these labels difficult to interpret. By translating rating symbols into familiar colour-coded risk categories, SEBI aims to make credit risk easier to assess.

Under the framework, credit ratings will be mapped to six risk categories. The first, Lowest Credit Risk, covers AAA-rated long-term debt securities and A1+-rated short-term instruments.

The second, Very Low Credit Risk, covers AA-rated securities, including the AA+ and AA- variants, and A1-rated short-term instruments.

The third, Low Credit Risk, includes A-rated securities and A2-rated short-term instruments.

BBB-rated securities fall under Moderate Credit Risk, alongside A3-rated short-term instruments. BB-rated securities are placed in the Moderate Risk of Default category, alongside A4+-rated short-term instruments.

The final category, High to Very High Risk of Default, covers B-, C- and D-rated securities, including their applicable rating modifiers, as well as A4- and D-rated short-term instruments. The colour spectrum progresses from green through yellow, brown and orange to red. The traffic-light format is designed to make differences in credit risk more immediately visible.

Where a CRA identifies an issuer as “Issuer Not Cooperating” (INC), the Credit Risk-o-Meter must indicate the INC status, with an arrow pointing towards it.

Issuers and OBPPs must additionally disclose the CRA’s name and the actual credit rating of the debt security in text below the meter. For unsecured debt instruments, the word “unsecured” must appear in bold red text. Where a security has ratings from multiple CRAs, the meter must reflect the lowest rating, although all ratings may be disclosed alongside it.

On mobile interfaces, the meter may be condensed, provided the entire risk spectrum remains visible and an arrow points to the product’s specific risk level. Selecting the information (‘i’) icon must bring up the detailed version, consistent with the web display.

What does it mean for investors?

Retail participation in bonds has grown alongside the emergence of online bond platforms, which allow investors to access corporate debt more conveniently. However, easier access does not necessarily mean investors fully understand the risks involved. A colour-coded meter could help bridge this gap by making the credit quality of a debt security easier to interpret at a glance.

SEBI has clarified that the meter reflects only credit risk and does not constitute investment advice or a recommendation to invest. It does not capture all the other risks associated with debt securities, including market and liquidity risks.

The distinction is particularly important for unsecured perpetual bonds, such as additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds issued by banks. SEBI has prescribed an additional disclaimer for these instruments, warning that the meter does not reflect their unique structural risks and that investors could lose their entire invested capital.

In essence, SEBI’s initiative seeks to make credit risk more visible. Investors can use the meter as a quick screening tool to understand where a security stands on the credit-risk spectrum. A green indicator signals a lower assessed credit risk, while orange and red indicate elevated risk. However, a lower credit-risk category does not automatically make a bond suitable for every investor. Yield, maturity, liquidity, issuer fundamentals, instrument structure and portfolio allocation must also be considered before investing.

data.title: Rising rates: What should your debt strategy be?
data.description:
In last week’s Big Story, we talked about why rising bond yields (and central banks hiking rates) globally, could represent a regime change for equity investors. As global interest rates climb after a prolonged phase of repression, investors may need to lower their return expectations from equities, at least at the market level. But there’s a positive side to this yield spike too — it opens up better return opportunities for debt investors.

In India, interest rates never went to zero. Therefore, the rise in yields poses less of a shock than in say, the US or Japan. However, with the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) restarting a rate hike cycle after a four-year gap, Indian debt investors may need to recalibrate their strategies to benefit from higher rates. To know what kind of bonds to own now, you need to gauge the direction of interest rates and the quantum of the change.

How market rates behaved

Today, whether you consider long-term interest rates or short-term, the direction is clearly up.

Long-term bond yields in India are pegged to the 10-year government security, which acts as the floor for long-term borrowing costs. After the Iran war broke out in February 2026 and oil prices surged, Indian bond markets worried about rising subsidies forcing the Central government to overshoot its deficit target. Therefore, the yield on longer-tenure Central government securities spiked first. Between January and April 2026, the yield on the 10-year G-Sec (government bond) rose from 6.6 per cent to 6.9 per cent. During this period, inflation remained low and there was no talk of policy rate hikes; so short-term interest rates stayed put.

With State governments on a borrowing binge, yields on SDLs (State government loans) spiked more, from 7.5 per cent to 7.9 per cent. Corporate bonds, which usually trade at a spread over G-Secs saw their yields increase. They rose from 7 per cent to 7.5 per cent for one-year AAA-rated bonds and 7.25 per cent to 7.6 per cent for three-year AAA-rated bonds. However, a frugal budget, which stayed with a 4.3 per cent fiscal deficit target in March and fuel price hikes in May, thereafter allayed fears about the deficit overshooting. Therefore, between April and October 2026, India’s 10-year government bond yields have risen only marginally from 6.9 per cent to 7.25 per cent.

However, yields on short-term bonds have played catch-up in this period. In recent months, it has become quite clear that a quick resolution to the Iran war is unlikely. Elevated energy prices and the long-lasting El Nino, have thus put upward pressure on domestic inflation, propping up CPI (consumer price index) inflation from 3.4 per cent in March to 4.8 per cent by August. This prompted bond markets to begin pricing in rate hikes by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC), with yields on 91-day to 364-day treasury bills rising from 5.3-5.6 per cent in April to 5.5-6.2 per cent now.

This week, the MPC met the market’s expectations by raising the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent. It also indicated that further rate hikes were in the offing, by talking of “calibrated tightening”.

What’s priced in

The above analysis shows that the direction of rates is pretty clear today. But how much will rates rise from here and how much of this is already priced into market yields? This is an important question because bond markets, like stock markets, price in events much before they happen.

On the first question, it is too early for a definitive answer. In the post-Covid rate hiking cycle that lasted from 2022 to 2023, the MPC hiked rates from 4 per cent to 6.5 per cent (250 basis points). In the extended cycle from 2010 to 2014, it hiked rates from 5 per cent all the way to 8 per cent, a 300-basis point hike. However, there have been shallower cycles too like 2017-18 when rates went up just 50 basis points from 6 per cent to 6.5 per cent. The quantum of hikes this time around will depend on incoming data on inflation, growth and capital flows. But it would be good to brace for an extended cycle.

On the second question of what the market is pricing in, the bond market seems to be pricing in another 70-75 basis points in rate hikes. One, the 364-day Treasury bill trades at about 6.28 per cent now, which is 78 basis points above the repo rate; T-bills yields have usually traded pretty close to the repo rate. Two, the 10-year G-Sec yield, at 7.23 per cent, is now 173 basis points above the repo rate. The average spread between the 10-year G-Sec and the repo has historically hovered at 80-100 basis points. This suggests that the additional 73 basis points is the market expectation for further rate increases.

Your debt strategy

This means three things for your debt strategy:

* With rate hikes just beginning, it may be risky to lock into bonds or debt mutual funds with long tenures (five years plus). Should market yields continue to shoot up or rate hikes go on for long, you can lose money by buying into long-duration bonds or debt funds today. In the past 15 years or so, 10-year G-Sec yields in India have topped out close to 8 per cent. Therefore, it would be good to wait for levels of 7.5-8 per cent on the 10-year G-Sec before considering long-duration bonds or debt funds. If you have surpluses to deploy now, it is safer today to invest them in bonds or debt funds with tenures of upto three years. This way, you can benefit from further rate hikes for as long as this cycle continues.

* Among three-year instruments, high-quality corporate bonds look attractive at yields of over 8 per cent. One- year and three-year AAA corporate bonds now trade at spreads of 142 and 125 basis points respectively over similar maturity G-Secs, which is high from a historical perspective. This makes such bonds a good buy. Currently, bonds from M&M Financial, Tata Capital, rated AAA and maturing in 2029, offer yields of about 8.1 per cent. PSU bonds from IRFC, HUDCO and SIDBI, maturing in 2029, offer about 7.65-7.8 per cent.

* While yields on G-Secs and corporate bonds are already factoring in the rise in policy rates, the fixed deposit market is yet to catch up. Large banks like SBI and ICICI still offer just 6.3-6.5 per cent for three-year deposits. Small finance banks, which traditionally offer the best FD deals, offer only 7.5-8 per cent, that too for special windows. Highly-rated NBFCs like Sundaram Finance and Bajaj Finance offer 7.25-7.75 per cent on three-year deposits. This could be due to banks enjoying comfortable liquidity after their FCNR (B) flows.

Debt investors fishing for higher returns today should thus stick to corporate bonds or debt mutual funds, opting for the shortest tenure possible within three years.

data.title: Fidelity’s Global Macro Director Jurrien Timmer Says Bitcoin Has Bottomed And Should Beat Gold Here On
data.description:
Key points:
  • Timmer said Bitcoin tested $60,000 before falling to $58,000, suggesting a bottom. He added that Bitcoin winters last 9 to 12 months.
  • He expects Bitcoin and gold to rise and said gold's fair value is $5,000, but speculators drove it to $5,600.
  • He said rising 10-year Treasury yields, around 5.3%, were pressuring stocks and causing a stealth correction. 

Bitcoin (BTC) has bottomed and should outperform gold from here, according to Fidelity Investments’ Jurrien Timmer. Timmer stated that Bitcoin ended a mild bear market, and its rise above $80,000 confirmed a double bottom, indicating that the price may have found support.

Timmer, the firm’s director of global macro, made the call during an appearance on The Compound & Friends podcast on Friday. Timmer said “60K is a level that I’m going to buy and it went to 58,” and that is a chart pattern in which a price tests a low twice and holds. He said the price looked right earlier this year, but the timing did not. Bitcoin’s winters have tended to last 9 to 12 months, he said. Traders often read it as a sign that a downtrend is over.

He expects both Bitcoin and gold to rally. He said there’s more room for Bitcoin to run. "Bitcoin is going to go up more," he said.

Cycle Model Missed Peak

His cycle model had pointed to a peak close to $150,000 last year, said Timmer. He said Bitcoin topped out at about $126,000. The model plots time and price on logarithmic scales, compressing large moves to make it easier to compare patterns. Each winter is shorter than the previous one, he said. “It’s a maturing asset, right? So, it’s going to moon less and it’s going to swoon less,” he said.

Timmer Says Gold Near $5,000: Warns Rising Treasury Yields Could Trigger Stock Correction

After Bitcoin’s peak, speculators moved out of Bitcoin into gold, Timmer said. That took gold to around $5,600, he said. His model of the global money supply indicates gold should not have risen above $4,800, he said. Fair value is about $5,000 and climbing, he added. Bitcoin priced in gold shows a double bottom too, he said.

Timmer’s take comes with a warning on bonds. The 10-year Treasury yield is around 5.3%, he said. He said rising yields are putting pressure on stocks and creating what he called a stealth correction.

He cited gold, Bitcoin and commodities as ways to diversify a portfolio when stocks and bonds fall together. Could those assets start trading in lockstep with stocks, the hosts asked. Some of them are in danger, he said.

Bitcoin’s price was trading around $82,935, flat over the past 24 hours. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘low’ levels over the past day.

data.title: Overseas ETFs: Nearly 30% of turnover at inflated prices
data.description:
With Indian equities delivering paltry returns over the past two-and-a-half years, many investors have turned to overseas markets in search of better opportunities. However, this shift towards global investments, particularly US technology and Artificial Intelligence (AI) stocks, has brought an unexpected risk.

Stark disconnect

An overseas exchange-traded fund (ETF) worth about ₹118 a unit traded at as much as ₹396 on Indian exchanges last month. The episode highlights a stark disconnect between market price and underlying value, undermining the low-cost appeal of passive investing.

The price distortion is not confined to one ETF but reflects a broader phenomenon across all six international ETFs.

Together, these funds recorded a turnover of ₹10,440 crore on the NSE and BSE so far in 2026, of which an estimated ₹3,094 crore involved trades at prices above net asset value (NAV), according to an analysis by bl.portfolio.

Motilal Oswal Nasdaq Q50 ETF’s market price surged from ₹142 on September 4 to ₹396.30 on September 18, against an NAV of ₹118.14, taking its premium to 235 per cent. Buyers were paying more than three times the underlying asset value, knowingly or otherwise. The ETF’s market price subsequently plunged to about ₹188 on September 28 before recovering to ₹252 by October 9. Its NAV, however, rose to ₹123.80 on October 9 from ₹118.14 on September 18. The sharp divergence illustrates how ETF prices can fluctuate dramatically without comparable movements in their underlying investments.

An analysis of market-price premiums over NAV across 21 trading sessions in the past month reveals wide divergences. Mirae Asset S&P 500 Top 50 ETF averaged a 49 per cent premium, peaking at 83 per cent. Mirae Asset NYSE FANG+ ETF averaged a 35 per cent premium, Mirae Asset Hang Seng TECH ETF 24 per cent and Motilal Oswal Nasdaq 100 ETF 17 per cent. Nippon India ETF Hang Seng BeES was relatively insulated, averaging a premium of 3 per cent.

By contrast, overseas ETFs tracking similar indices traded at premiums or discounts ranging from a marginal 0.01 per cent discount to a 15 per cent premium. China’s Guotai Nasdaq-100 ETF traded at a 15 per cent premium to NAV, while South Korea’s Samsung KODEX US NASDAQ 100 ETF traded at a 0.01 per cent discount. South Africa’s Satrix S&P 500 ETF and China Southern S&P 500 ETF traded at premiums of 0.3 per cent and 8.6 per cent, respectively.

Trading surge

The six ETFs recorded about 25.3 lakh trades across the NSE and BSE during the 21-session period. Elevated trading activity, sharp price swings and steep premiums point to intense short-term speculation.

Jatin Vasaria, Head of Products, Passive Funds, Motilal Oswal AMC, said the Motilal Oswal Nasdaq Q50 ETF, which previously recorded daily trading volumes of around ₹4-5 crore on a good day, suddenly saw volumes jump to ₹50-60 crore. Such activity was unusual for the fund, he said.

The surge suggests that some traders who entered during the initial rally may have booked profits as prices corrected, while fresh buying may have supported the subsequent recovery.

Supply squeeze

The distortion stems from overseas investment limits of $7 billion for overseas securities and $1 billion for overseas ETFs. These caps have constrained domestic fund houses from creating fresh units despite sustained demand for global equities.

Normally, authorised participants create or redeem ETF units to keep market prices aligned with NAV through arbitrage. Restrictions on fresh unit creation weaken this mechanism, allowing premiums to widen when demand outstrips supply.

The sharp price movements have also coincided with changes to the framework governing ETF trading bands. Following SEBI’s June 15 circular, exchanges implemented revised trading parameters from September 7, changing the reference used to determine permissible price movements. Previously, the reference NAV was from two trading days earlier (T-2). Under the revised mechanism, the base price is linked to the previous trading day’s closing price. This may have enabled sharper price movements in ETFs already facing supply constraints.

SEBI has also asked exchanges and asset management companies to work towards adopting the previous trading day’s closing NAV as the base price from April 1, 2027.

The unusual premiums have prompted warnings from both the NSE and BSE. They could narrow if overseas investment limits are raised, allowing fund houses to create fresh units, or as changes to the T-1 NAV-based price-band framework take effect.

For investors, the risk is two-fold: A decline in overseas markets and an erosion of the premium paid to acquire ETF units. Even if the underlying securities hold their value, a sharp contraction in the premium could cause substantial losses for investors who buy at elevated market prices.

Regulatory changes could eventually ease these distortions, potentially triggering a swift and sharp correction in ETF prices.

data.title: Philips investors’ move to probe company over 2021 recall denied by Dutch court
data.description:
A court in Amsterdam on Saturday denied demands by shareholders of Philips for an investigation into the company over its handling of a massive product recall involving its sleep apnea and ventilator machines in 2021.

The Enterprise Chamber of the Amsterdam Court of Appeal ruled in favor of the company, dealing a setback to a large group of Philips shareholders, including the Dutch investors’ association, VEB, and several institutional investors.

The shareholders called for a court inquiry after the Dutch medtech launched a recall of roughly 3.5M breathing machines in 2021 due to concerns that a polyurethane foam used in the devices could deteriorate and become toxic.

The investors argued that the company failed to identify and address the issues promptly due to weaknesses in its internal systems, the chambers said. They also alleged that the Philips board of directors was aware of the problems at the company’s Respironics U.S. unit, which made the devices, well before the disclosures were made regarding the issue.

“There is also no reason to assume that Philips ought to have intervened at Respironics earlier, or that the Supervisory Board exercised insufficient oversight,” Bloomberg reported, quoting the chamber. It added that there is no sufficient basis to determine that Philips' disclosures to the investors were “late, incorrect, or misleading.”

The chamber didn’t rule on whether there were errors at Respironics or regarding the extent of liability for damages faced by investors.

data.title: RBI may hike repo rate by 75-100 bps in current cycle as inflation persists- SBI Capital flags December hike risk
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) may raise the repo rate by 75-100 basis points during the current monetary tightening cycle, as inflationary pressures are expected to persist before easing in the next financial year, according to a report by SBI Capital Markets.

The brokerage said gradual rate increases remain the most likely scenario, although a larger hike in December 2026 cannot be ruled out. The RBI's decision will depend on inflation readings for September and October.

The Monetary Policy Committee's 25-basis-point repo rate hike and its shift in monetary policy stance from "Neutral" to "Calibrated Tightening" indicate a stronger emphasis on controlling inflation, the report said.

SBI Capital Markets expects the monetary policy cycle to reverse in the first quarter of FY28, depending on how the balance between economic growth and inflation evolves.

Retail inflation may peak in Q3 FY27

Consumer price inflation is expected to peak in the third quarter of FY27, while wholesale price inflation could begin moderating from March 2027 as favourable base effects come into play.

The report expects retail inflation to remain below 5% year-on-year beyond the first quarter of FY28, suggesting that price pressures could gradually ease in the next financial year.

However, the trajectory will depend on domestic inflation trends, global commodity prices and geopolitical developments.

India's economic growth remained robust in the first quarter of FY27, with real gross domestic product (GDP) expanding 7.8% year-on-year, surpassing market expectations of 7.1%.

Manufacturing output grew 9.2% during the quarter, while gross fixed capital formation, an indicator of investment activity, increased 11.9%.

Despite the strong growth figures, SBI Capital Markets flagged potential risks to consumption in the second half of FY27. Rising borrowing costs, subdued rural sentiment and weaker kharif sowing could weigh on consumer demand.

The brokerage also warned that prolonged geopolitical conflicts and crude oil prices hovering around $100 per barrel could sustain inflationary pressures and increase costs across the economy.

Benchmark 10-year government bond yields have risen by around 70 basis points in calendar year 2026, reflecting concerns over inflation, monetary tightening and global financial conditions.

According to the report, bond yields are likely to remain elevated until geopolitical tensions ease and inflationary pressures moderate.

Rising yields in advanced economies and capital outflows from emerging markets are adding to financial market uncertainty, increasing pressure on domestic borrowing costs.

Higher interest rates are expected to support bank margins in the near term, although non-food credit growth could gradually lose momentum towards the end of FY27.

SBI Capital Markets expects FY27 to remain favourable for the banking sector, while bonds could regain investor interest in FY28 as inflationary pressures ease and the monetary policy cycle potentially turns more accommodative.

The outlook for both banks and bond markets will depend on the pace of rate hikes, the trajectory of inflation and developments in global financial markets.

data.title: DMart's Q2 profit growth trails revenue as expenses rise
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Avenue Supermarts Ltd, which runs the DMart retail chain, reported a 17.8% year-on-year rise in consolidated revenue to Rs.19,644 crore in the July-September quarter, driven by stronger growth at older stores and continued expansion across India.

Consolidated net profit rose 8.5% to Rs.743 crore in the second quarter of FY27, slower than revenue growth. The company's net profit margin narrowed to 3.8% from 4.1% a year earlier, while its earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda) margin declined to 7.1% from 7.3%.

The Mumbai-based retailer added 15 stores during the quarter, taking its total count to 518 as of 30 September. The company said entry-level wage inflation had led to a marginal increase in operating expenses, even as it remained committed to its value-for-money pricing strategy.

A key highlight of the quarter was stronger growth at older stores. "Two years and older DMart stores grew by 9.5% during Q2 FY27 as compared to 6.8% in Q2 FY26," said Anshul Asawa, managing director and chief executive officer of Avenue Supermarts.

Operating expenses reflected the pressure of higher costs. Consolidated employee benefits expense rose 18.7% year-on-year to Rs.447.14 crore, while finance costs jumped 82.8% to Rs.63.90 crore. Depreciation and amortisation expenses increased 25.4% to Rs.317.75 crore, and other expenses rose 18.3% to Rs.1,091.83 crore.

Food and grocery products continued to dominate the retailer's sales mix. They accounted for 56.9% of revenue in the first half of FY27, while general merchandise and apparel contributed 23.6%, and non-food fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) accounted for 19.5%. The share of general merchandise and apparel edged up from 23.3% in the year-earlier period, while the share of food and non-food FMCG was broadly stable.

The company continued to follow its everyday low-cost, everyday low-price model, which focuses on sourcing products competitively and leveraging operational and distribution efficiencies to offer lower prices. It did not provide forward-looking guidance on revenue growth or store additions in its results announcement.

DMart's online grocery and essentials platform, DMart Ready, operated in 11 cities in the first half of FY27, down from 19 in the corresponding period a year ago, according to the company's investor presentation.

The subsidiary reported a net loss of Rs.75.35 crore in the September quarter and Rs.166.62 crore in the first half of FY27, according to the consolidated financial statements. The company's presentation showed DMart Ready's presence in 11 cities during the first half, although the results announcement did not separately detail the online business's financial performance.

"We are focused on driving greater operational efficiencies and strengthening overall customer experience in the cities that we currently operate in," said Vikram Dasu, whole-time director and chief executive officer of Avenue E-Commerce Ltd, which operates DMart Ready.

The platform faces competition from quick-commerce companies such as Blinkit and Swiggy Instamart, which have expanded their dark-store networks to enable faster deliveries. DMart Ready's focus on operational efficiency and customer experience comes as the company concentrates its online operations in fewer cities.

Based in Mumbai, she will lead marketing and omnichannel media for the company’s drinkware business. Bhushan brings experience spanning digital strategy, media planning and buying, client management and campaign execution, having worked across advertising and media agencies including DDB Mudra Group, Madison World, Mindshare and Span Digital.

Roles Across Agencies

Bhushan worked as Business Director at Madison World from July 2018 to November 2020. In that role, she handled digital and client responsibilities for Tata Consumer Products, Welspun and other accounts, covering brand communication, media planning and buying, campaign ideation and client servicing.

Earlier, she worked as Director– Digital at Mindshare between May 2017 and January 2018, handling media planning and buying for clients including Castrol, Star India and Facebook. Her responsibilities included market and competition analysis, pitch presentations and digital initiatives.

From May 2015 to April 2017, Bhushan was Senior Account Director– Digital at Span Digital. She led client servicing, digital strategy and media planning across public- and private-sector accounts, with work spanning display, mobile, social media, search, performance marketing and website initiatives.

Focus On Omnichannel Media

At Hamilton Housewares, Bhushan’s role covers marketing and omnichannel media for drinkware. The appointment brings agency-side experience in digital planning and buying into a role focused on a consumer products business.

Omnichannel marketing connects brand communication and consumer engagement across digital and physical touchpoints. For consumer goods companies, the approach can bring media planning, brand visibility and purchasing journeys into closer alignment. Bhushan’s experience across digital strategy and integrated media is relevant to this remit.

Bhushan holds a postgraduate diploma in management, specialising in marketing and human resources, from the Institute of Management Studies, Ghaziabad. She completed the programme in 2010 after earning a bachelor’s degree in English and economics from Isabella Thoburn College.

data.title: Mansi M. Moves From Unilever To Lead Marketing At Epigamia
data.description:
The marketing leader moves from Unilever to focus on brand building, product innovation and business growth at the premium dairy company

Mansi M. joined Epigamia as Head of Marketing in October 2026, moving from Unilever after more than nine years with the consumer goods company. With over 14 years of experience across Britannia, Airtel and Unilever, her career spans sales and distribution, trade marketing, brand management and business leadership. At Epigamia, she will focus on strengthening the brand, driving innovation, expanding digital and e-commerce capabilities, and building the marketing team as the company pursues its ambition of becoming India’s most preferred premium value-added dairy brand.

Experience Across Functions

Before joining Epigamia, Mansi led brand and business growth for OZiva at Unilever as Senior Marketing Manager from August 2025 to October 2026. Her responsibilities included brand positioning, product development, campaign strategy, e-commerce and quick commerce growth, and pricing and profitability decisions. She also held P&L responsibility, balancing brand investment with commercial performance.

Between August 2023 and August 2025, she worked as Brand Manager for OZiva, leading a packaging and visual identity transformation, portfolio premiumisation and offline expansion. Her work included developing the route-to-market strategy, channel-specific portfolios and pricing architecture to support the brand’s expansion beyond online channels.

Building Sales Channels

Mansi joined Unilever in 2017 after working at Airtel as Product Manager and Assistant Manager for Sales and Distribution. At Unilever, she held roles in key account management and trade marketing before becoming Area Sales Manager for the pharmaceutical channel in August 2021.

In that role, she established the company’s pharmaceutical channel model, building its go-to-market structure, distributor network, organisational design and sales processes. She also led a cross-functional team of key account executives and territory leads as the model expanded nationally.

Earlier, she worked at Britannia Industries in trade marketing and sales development from 2012 to 2014, focusing on point-of-sale initiatives, distribution expansion and go-to-market planning.

Focus On Brand Growth

At Epigamia, Mansi’s remit includes developing campaigns and storytelling to strengthen brand distinctiveness, identifying opportunities for product innovation and improving the connection between consumer demand and e-commerce and digital commerce. She will also work on building a team focused on experimentation, execution and commercial outcomes.

Her stated approach to marketing emphasises combining creativity with measurable business impact, using data and experience to inform decisions while remaining open to new ideas. Her transition brings experience across established consumer brands and a wellness business to Epigamia as it seeks to expand its reach in the value-added dairy market.

The appointment marks a shift from leading the growth of a wellness brand within a large consumer goods organisation to taking on a marketing leadership role at a dedicated food brand, with brand building and business growth forming the core of her new responsibilities.

data.title: FMCG players expect emerging distribution channels to post strong growth for Q2 FY27
data.description:
Leading FMCG players witnessed strong growth momentum in alternative distribution channels which includes quick commerce, e-commerce and modern trade. In recent quarters, FMCG players have been reporting strong acceleration in sales in the overall e-commerce channel led by quick-commerce platforms.

As per quarterly update for Q2FY27, AWL Agribusiness indicated that alternate channel, consisting of modern trade, quick-commerce and e-commerce, delivered “double-digit growth”. “Within food & FMCG, key categories continued to gain traction across e-commerce and quick commerce, collectively delivering 40 per cent year-on-year growth. AWL has established a meaningful presence across these channels, with average market shares of over 10 per cent in Atta, over 25 per cent in Besan, over 40 per cent in Soya Nuggets, and around 15–20 per cent across Sugar, Suji and Poha,” the company added. It also said that execution metrics such as product fill rate and customer retention saw improvement during the quarter, supported by better assortment and availability.

In a BSE filing, Dabur India noted that “emerging channels comprising e-commerce and quick commerce are expected to report “strong growth momentum” in Q2FY27, led by its continued investments and focus on an omni-channel distribution approach. “Modern trade continues to grow at double digits. General trade continued to grow across both urban and rural markets, with rural continuing to outpace urban, led by continued efforts under Project Saksham,” the company added.

Honasa Consumer Ltd, known for brands such as Mamaearth, also noted in its Q2 update that the online channel witnessed “continued growth” momentum during the quarter. It added that general trade and modern trade channels are also expected to post strong growth on the back of its focus on garnering deeper offline distribution.

According to estimates by NielsenIQ, the overall e-commerce channel’s share grew to 7 per cent of pan-India FMCG sales in the June quarter. E-commerce channel share of FMCG sales in the top eight metros was pegged at 21 per cent. At the same time in the top 52 metros, the online channel’s share of industry sales was estimated at 21 per cent in the June quarter.

data.title: PM Narendra Modi in Chennai on Sunday for a series of engagements
data.description:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be in Chennai on Sunday October 11 for a series of events including the flag off of a new section of the Chennai Metro and inauguration of projects.

As per an official government statement, at around 11.30 am, he will undertake a ride on the Chennai Metro from Porur Bypass Station to Poonamallee Bypass Station and back. He will likely be joined by TN CM Joseph Vijay for this ride. He will also inaugurate the new Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around ₹4,900 crore.

Then, he will perform Darshan and Pooja at the Jalakandeswarar Temple in Chennai. Thereafter, he will take a walkthrough of the Brain Centre at IIT Madras.

This will be followed by the Prime Minister laying the foundation stone , inaugurating and dedicating various development projects worth over ₹13,000 crore. He will also address the gathering at this occasion.

Finally, the PM will also participate in the Golden Jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School in Chennai.

inaugurate projects

He will lay the foundation stone of and inaugurate key National Highway projects worth around ₹3,700 crore.

Prime Minister will dedicate and inaugurate railway infrastructure projects worth over ₹750 crore.

He will also inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of several port-related projects in Tamil Nadu to strengthen maritime infrastructure, expand cargo-handling capacity and improve logistics efficiency. This includes four infrastructure projects at Chennai Port: a Paved Storage Yard, four EXIM Godowns, an upgraded Cruise Terminal and a Seafarers Club.

Further, PM Modi will lay the foundation stone of the Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) project at the existing Manali Refinery of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd (CPCL) in Chennai. With a total cost of around ₹1,620 crore and a capacity of 270 thousand tonnes per annum , the project aims to produce Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks for the manufacture of world-class, premium-quality lubricants in India.

At the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre (SGBC) at IIT Madras, he is also set to launch its pioneering global scientific mission to map more than 100 human brains into three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution, across the human lifespan — from the foetal stage to old age.

data.title: Ether ETFs extend outflow streak to nine days as Solana funds snap record 14-week inflow run
data.description:
U.S. spot ether (ETH) ETFs recorded $542.1 million in net outflows last week, their worst week since January, while spot Solana (SOL) ETFs ended a record 14-week inflow streak, according to The Block's analysis of SoSoValue data.

The ether funds have now posted outflows for nine consecutive trading days, a run worth $697.2 million that began on Sept. 29.

Spot Solana ETFs lost $24.8 million over the week, the largest weekly outflow since the products launched in late October 2025.

Combined with bitcoin ETF redemptions, the three categories lost about $1.25 billion last week.

Ether funds post second straight losing week

BlackRock's ETHA, the largest ether fund by assets under management, lost $477.0 million over the week, about 88% of the category's total, per SoSoValue data. It was the fund's largest weekly outflow since mid-December 2025 and its third-largest since launching in July 2024. Grayscale's ETHE had the second-largest weekly outflow among ether funds, at $31.9 million.

Tuesday was the heaviest single trading day for the ether products, with $201.9 million in redemptions, all from ETHA. That was the fund's largest single-day outflow since Jan. 21 of this year. Tuesday's outflow came on the day ETHA's 1-for-3 reverse share split took effect.

ETHA posted outflows in all five sessions. The fund holds $8.64 billion in net assets, about $4.15 billion less than its $12.79 billion in cumulative net inflows.

The category's weekly total outflows were the largest since the week ending Jan. 23, when the funds lost $611.2 million. It was also the second straight negative week for ether ETFs, after $138.0 million left the funds the week before. Fidelity's FETH accounted for $74.1 million of that prior-week total, per the data.

Daily ether ETF flows have been negative in every session since Sept. 28, when the funds took in $17.1 million. The ether outflows began on Sept. 29, one day before bitcoin ETFs ended a nine-day, $3.1 billion inflow streak. ETHA accounted for $506.1 million of the nine-day streak's outflows.

The run ties a June 17-30 streak as the third-longest in the funds' history. The record is a 17-day stretch from May 11 to June 3 of this year, which pulled about $900.1 million from the products.

Spot ether ETF net assets fell 10% over the week to $15.71 billion. Cumulative net inflows since launch stand at $13.26 billion. The funds are still positive for 2026, with $931.8 million in net inflows year to date, down from $1.47 billion a week earlier.

Trading volume rose to $5.18 billion from $3.57 billion the previous week.

Solana funds end record inflow run

The Solana products recorded outflows in all five sessions last week, their longest daily outflow streak on record, per SoSoValue's data. Their previous longest outflow streak was three days.

Bitwise's BSOL, the largest Solana fund with $1.20 billion in net assets, lost $20.9 million over the week, about 84% of the category's outflows, per the data. It was BSOL's largest weekly outflow on record, topping a $17.0 million outflow in the week ending July 31.

Monday's $9.2 million outflow was the largest of the week. Morgan Stanley's MSOL and Invesco's QSOL were the only Solana funds to post weekly inflows, taking in a combined $2.0 million.

The $24.8 million weekly outflow is roughly three times the previous record of $8.9 million, set in the week ending Feb. 6. The funds had not posted a negative week since the week ending June 26, when they lost $1.8 million. The 14-week inflow streak topped a 13-week run that started at launch and ended in late January.

The reversal comes two weeks after the Solana funds drew a record $188.2 million in weekly inflows.

Spot Solana ETF net assets fell to $1.73 billion from $1.90 billion a week earlier. The funds held a record $1.96 billion on Sept. 25. Cumulative net inflows stand at $1.58 billion, including $816.8 million so far in 2026.

Bitcoin funds snap three-week inflow streak

Spot bitcoin (BTC) ETFs lost $681.1 million last week, ending three straight weeks of inflows, per SoSoValue data. It was their worst week since the week ending June 26, when they shed $1.79 billion.

Wednesday accounted for most of the outflows, with $487.1 million leaving the funds. The products returned to inflows on Friday with $21.1 million.

The bitcoin funds' 2026 net inflows fell to $494.1 million from $1.18 billion a week earlier. The category turned positive for the year in late September.

Bitcoin ETFs hold $105.84 billion in net assets and have drawn $57.11 billion in cumulative net inflows since launch.

Ether traded near $2,506 on Saturday morning, while SOL changed hands around $110.50 and bitcoin sat near $82,900.

data.title: Indian stock markets snap 8-week losing streak - What's next for Sensex, Nifty? Triggers, strategy ​for investors
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Indian equity markets ended their eight-week losing streak, the longest in 25 years, after a volatile week in which benchmarks recovered on buying in information technology (IT), fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), automobile and financial stocks. However, persistent foreign fund outflows, elevated crude oil prices, rising global bond yields and uncertainty over the monetary policy outlook continued to weigh on investor sentiment.

For the week, the BSE Sensex gained 562.63 points, or 0.78%, to close at 72,472.33, while the Nifty 50 advanced 98.5 points, or 0.43%, to settle at 22,520.45.

The recovery gathered momentum on Friday, October 9, when the Sensex surged 879.09 points, or 1.23%, to 72,472.33. The Nifty 50 climbed 288.65 points, or 1.30%, to end at 22,520.45, snapping the benchmarks' eight-week losing streak.

"Markets snapped an eight-week losing streak, posting modest weekly gains as easing crude oil prices and positive corporate updates supported a late-week recovery. However, volatility remained elevated following the RBI's decision to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and shift its policy stance towards calibrated tightening," said Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research, Religare Broking.

Despite the rebound, market participants will look for stronger follow-through buying to determine whether the recovery can extend into the coming week. Several domestic and global developments, including inflation data, corporate earnings, crude oil prices and foreign investor flows, are likely to influence the market's direction.

Inflation data from the US will be a key trigger for global equity markets next week. US consumer inflation, core inflation, producer price inflation (PPI) and retail-sales figures will offer fresh cues on the health of the economy and the likely trajectory of the Federal Reserve's monetary policy.

Stronger-than-expected inflation readings could keep US Treasury yields and the dollar elevated, potentially putting pressure on emerging-market equities.

Crude oil remains one of the most important macroeconomic variables for Indian equities because of its implications for the country's import bill, inflation, corporate margins and currency.

Brent crude was trading above $100 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) was above $90, according to the market assessment provided. Uncertainty surrounding Iran, the Strait of Hormuz and regional energy infrastructure has also raised concerns about possible supply disruptions.

A sustained increase in crude oil prices could put pressure on India's external balance and the rupee, while raising input and transportation costs for companies. This could complicate the inflation outlook and affect expectations around interest rates.

Investors will also track September consumer price inflation (CPI) and wholesale price inflation (WPI) data in India for indications of domestic price pressures and their implications for monetary policy.

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) remained net sellers for the seventh consecutive week, offloading equities worth Rs.30,294.29 crore. Domestic institutional investors (DIIs), meanwhile, purchased equities worth Rs.30,313.48 crore during the week, providing a cushion against overseas selling.

Persistent FII outflows remain an overhang for the market, particularly if global bond yields stay elevated or the dollar strengthens. At the same time, continued domestic institutional buying could help absorb some of the selling pressure and limit further declines.

Currency movements will remain important as well. The Indian rupee depreciated by 41 paise during the week ended October 9 to close at 96.73 against the US dollar, compared with 96.32 on October 1. It traded in a range of 96.22-96.85 during the week, moving closer to its all-time low of 96.96.

Continued rupee weakness could add to imported inflation and influence foreign investor sentiment.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) recently raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and shifted its policy stance towards calibrated tightening. While the rate increase was broadly in line with expectations, the change in stance has raised concerns about borrowing costs and the possibility of further policy action.

The RBI's upward revision of its FY27 GDP growth forecast, however, provided some reassurance about the resilience of the domestic economy.

IT stocks led Friday's market recovery after Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) reported its September-quarter results, helping lift the broader indices.

Attention will now shift to HCL Technologies, Wipro and Tech Mahindra, whose quarterly results and management commentary could influence sentiment towards the sector.

Investors will look for updates on demand conditions, client spending, deal momentum, margins and business outlook. Strong corporate commentary could help sustain the rebound in IT stocks, while cautious guidance could limit gains.

The broader September-quarter earnings season will also gather momentum, with Hero MotoCorp and Nestle India among the companies scheduled to announce results. Their performance and commentary on demand, input costs and margins will provide further insight into corporate earnings trends.

The end of the eight-week losing streak marks a break in the recent downward trend, but it does not by itself confirm a sustained market reversal. Elevated crude oil prices, foreign investor selling and global macroeconomic uncertainty continue to pose risks.

Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research at Religare Broking, identified the 22,200-22,400 zone as a crucial support area to monitor. According to Mishra, holding above this region could support a recovery towards 23,000-23,300. Conversely, a decisive break below the support zone could trigger renewed weakness towards 21,700-22,000.

These levels will be important for traders assessing whether the recent rebound has enough strength to continue. Market breadth and buying participation across sectors will also help determine whether the gains extend beyond selective buying and short-covering.

"Traders should remain selective, avoid excessive leverage and adhere to disciplined risk management. Investors should prioritise companies with resilient earnings, strong balance sheets and pricing power, while considering staggered accumulation at appropriate valuations," suggested the expert.

The coming week will be important in determining whether the recovery can gain traction after the Nifty and Sensex ended their eight-week losing streak. India's September CPI and WPI inflation data, US inflation and retail-sales figures, corporate earnings, crude oil prices and geopolitical developments will be among the key triggers, noted Mishra.

Investors will also track FII and DII activity, rupee movements and US Treasury yields for signs of whether the broader risk environment is improving.

data.title: Hospital group files lawsuit to stop 340B rebate pilot again
data.description:
The American Hospital Association has once again filed a lawsuit to halt a new pilot that tests a revised rebate model for the 340B Drug Pricing Program, a federal benefits program for underinsured and low-income Americans.

The AHA, the Maine Hospital Association, and four safety-net hospitals filed the suit on Thursday, naming the Health and Human Services Department and the Health Resources and Services Administration, the HHS unit overseeing the program, among its defendants.

The lawsuit was filed in a federal court in Maine days after the HRSA announced the pilot, which allows 10 pharmaceutical manufacturers to offer after-the-fact rebates instead of upfront discounts on 21 drugs purchased under the program.

The Trump administration’s first 340B rebate pilot, which applied to only 10 medicines, was blocked by a federal judge in December following a lawsuit from the AHA and several hospital systems. The HHS formally withdrew the plan in January after losing on appeal.

The latest complaint seeks a temporary and permanent block on the program, which is set to take effect on Jan. 1 with the participation of drugmakers including AbbVie , Amgen , Astellas , AstraZeneca , Bristol Myers , GSK , Merck , Pfizer , and Teva .

It makes arguments similar to the first, noting that the pilot doesn’t account for substantial costs the providers will have to incur by purchasing the drugs at market prices and then applying for rebates.

Listed hospital systems: HCA Healthcare , Community Health Systems , Surgery Partners , Tenet Healthcare , Universal Health Services , Select Medical Holdings (SEM), Acadia Healthcare , LifeStance Health Group
